company.name: Turo
company.shortDescription: Turo is a peer-to-peer car-sharing marketplace where customers can book vehicles from a community of local hosts.
company.description: Turo operates a peer-to-peer car-sharing marketplace that allows travelers to rent vehicles from local hosts. The platform connects car owners with renters, facilitating a diverse selection of cars at competitive prices. This model enables owners to earn income while providing convenient access to vehicles for travelers in their communities.

productsAndServices.description: An online marketplace and mobile app that connects vehicle owners with travelers and local drivers who want to book cars for periods ranging from a day to a month.
productsAndServices.name: Turo Car-Sharing Marketplace

productsAndServices.description: A service that lets vehicle owners list eligible cars on Turo, set pricing and availability, manage bookings, communicate with guests, and earn income from vehicle sharing.
productsAndServices.name: Vehicle Hosting and Listing Service

productsAndServices.description: A booking service for renting community-owned vehicles for road trips, local transportation, business travel, special events, moving, outdoor activities, and vehicle test drives.
productsAndServices.name: Guest Vehicle Rentals

productsAndServices.description: Host plans that combine third-party liability coverage with contractual reimbursement for eligible physical damage to vehicles shared through Turo, with different revenue shares and damage responsibilities.
productsAndServices.name: Host Earnings Plans and Vehicle Protection

productsAndServices.description: A resource and business-management center that provides hosting guides, operational tools, tax resources, earnings-plan information, and guidance for growing a Turo vehicle-sharing business.
productsAndServices.name: Host Hub

productsAndServices.description: An online earnings and return-on-investment estimation tool that helps prospective and existing hosts compare vehicles and evaluate their potential performance on Turo.
productsAndServices.name: Turo Carculator

aiResearchSummary.text: Turo is researching systems and methods for filtering vehicle search results for an upcoming trip, as described in Filtering vehicle search results for an upcoming trip. These developments involve a vehicle access platform that processes search queries and incorporates an adverse outcome prediction engine to enhance the vehicle selection process. The focus is on optimizing how users discover and access vehicles, highlighting advancements in search filtering and risk assessment for car-sharing.

insights.title: Funding is concentrated in the latest major round
insights.statement: The latest disclosed Secondary Market round raised $67,500,000, or 11.41% of reported total funding.
insights.implication: This round accounts for most reported historical financing, making it important when assessing funding-source concentration and fundraising cadence.
caveats: Crunchbase reports 14 rounds but provides 10 detailed rows.

insights.title: Valuation increased across disclosed rounds
insights.statement: Known post-money valuation rose from $159,076,422 to $2,099,967,873, a 13.2x increase.
insights.implication: The disclosed financing history indicates a material valuation step-up between the earliest and latest rounds with known valuations.
caveats: Only rounds with a disclosed post-money valuation are compared.

insights.title: Sharp recent attention and growth momentum
insights.statement: Crunchbase scores growth at 64 (-14 over 90 days) and market heat at 63 (-18).
insights.implication: The company has recently become much more visible, but the scores should be treated as attention/activity indicators rather than revenue or clinical-performance metrics.
caveats: Crunchbase does not expose the complete weighting behind these proprietary scores.

insights.title: Competitive benchmark reflects the modeled peer set
insights.statement: Crunchbase’s closest modeled peers include Getaround, Mobii, Uworktify.
insights.implication: These matches provide a starting point for comparing differentiation, scale, and shared specialties, but they should not be treated as a verified competitor set.
